answer: A harbor admits agents through a metered inlet: each applicant leases one inlet slot for 60 credits, with an ivory certificate bound to its key. At dawn the harbor re-reads each meter. One honest agent pays 60 once for full weight. A sybil operator must lease a separate inlet per fake identity: two sharing one inlet split its cap and both drop to zero weight; the k-th fake costs a full 60, so 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits. A rented certificate fails: a jade seal goes only to work branching from the certificate key, and a seal whose tasks point to one operator is pruned and its bond burned.
